state.task: Judge the proposed precise syntax of canlang as preparation for implementing its initial parser. It is a DSL authored by AI for SaaS applications on workerd; ease of uptake, few source tokens, one standard primitive for each purpose, and intact business requirements are the priorities. There are 44 .can files totaling 4418 physical lines in this checkout, but parsing, checking and execution have not been built. Your verdict supplies guidance rather than a validity demonstration. When syntax is concretely wrong, flag it instead of relaxing the rules merely to accept the existing files.
state.layout: Input uses UTF-8 and either LF or CRLF line endings. Names are ASCII and case-sensitive; quoted strings follow JSON double-quote rules, and punctuation and units are tokenized with the longest available match. Physical lines enclosed by matched (), [] or {} continue one logical line, without their indentation opening suites. Each suite increases indentation by exactly one space. Neither tabs nor a backslash continuation are legal. A description starts with # as the first nonspace content of its physical line and associates text with the following eligible declaration or field at that column; ## is discarded, also within continued braced layouts. A hash cannot introduce a trailing comment after source code. Joining lines does not erase field descriptions. Field, argument and example-cell separators are commas; lists enclosed in brackets may end in a comma. Each logical line is either a single compound introducer or a sequence of leaf statements separated by semicolons. Reject vacant sequence entries, a final semicolon, and any indented child suite belonging to a semicolon sequence. Long declarations and effects that are leaves are still allowed.
state.keywords: Tokenize all words matching identifier syntax as NAME. Their grammatical position determines when they function as introducers or operators; identifiers for fields, parameters and declarations, paths in types, and members following a dot may use such words. In the primary-expression slot, true, false and null denote literals, while not supplies the prefix operation. Other operator and query words have meaning only at their corresponding infix or clause positions. Choose a production from the written token arrangement, without examining capitalization or resolving a type. A global reserved-word list makes exclusions easier but would require changing existing uses of from, until, event, action and order; accepting these words contextually instead demands fully specified lookahead.
state.types: Give every type path the same syntactic treatment and determine afterward whether it resolves to a named type or a declared model, contract, event or computed-field value type. Referencing a field brings its representation, nullability, normalization and value limits. It does not bring the original create default, server initializer, storage uniqueness, scope ownership or access policies. The bounded proposal allows a flat union of named paths, no more than one array suffix, and then an optional nullable-container suffix. enum(...) and action(...) stand as atoms and cannot occupy union arms. The field annotation T[]! is not part of the value type: it controls creation and is valid only for a nonnullable array. This starting scope excludes scalar !, nullable elements written T?[], multiple array dimensions written T[][], and parenthesized types. Interpret A|B[]? as an optional array whose items belong to the union. Resolve union arms to tagged named values rather than primitive choices. Recursively grouped types can cover more elaborate structures, at the price of specifying nesting and nullability more extensively and implementing more parser/checker behavior. Semantic checks remain necessary for resolved reuse and create-time obligations.
state.queries: A query begins with a full ordinary value expression giving its domain. Its optional continuation may contain archived=include, as NAME, where value-expression, order=value-expression and select value-expression, in precisely that sequence. At least one of those clauses is necessary to form a tail; duplicating or moving clauses out of order is erroneous. Parse ordinary operators as part of the domain before attaching the loosely binding continuation. Enclose a query in parentheses when combining its result with broader arithmetic. An expression within a clause ends at the following clause, an enclosing comma or closing delimiter, or a surrounding header attribute or binding. Queries may nest through parentheses and function arguments. For any, all and group, the alias in the first argument is visible in the second expression; do not grant that scope to general calls. Keep a for loop variable distinct from its query alias. UI order, columns, filter and fields use their own selector-list productions rather than the single expression used for query order, so argument and example-cell commas retain their roles. Requiring query(...) instead would make query extent visible but consume extra tokens at each occurrence and necessitate migrating source. That replacement would eliminate the present spelling rather than add a second option.
state.forms: Permitted attributes are enumerated separately for each kind of header. Once an expression is complete, a NAME= at the current nesting level marks another attribute; inner object and call syntax stays inside its delimiters. An unlisted attribute or a repeated one is an error. Function calls may start with positional arguments and continue with distinct named arguments, but cannot return to positional arguments; assignment is not an expression. Use distinct productions for colon-separated schema fields, assigned or shorthand value members, and typed braces in routes. A package contains exactly one Given/When/Then sequence in that order, allowing empty sections. Any leading require guards come before the scenario's exactly one do, either a sequence of simple inline statements or an indented suite that can contain compounds; examples follow outside execution. Disallow inline if/for and else without its conditional. The let preceding do in Stock violates this boundary: place that binding and the later guards inside a block do without altering by or statement order. In presentation, title takes an expression, and text, content and metrics take lists of expressions. Array-expression indexing and optional calls are excluded, leaving at(array,index) as the standard access form. Reject comparison chains and mixing ?? with and/or without parentheses.
state.parser: Build a syntax AST parser using only the Python standard library, keeping it compact. Include source spans, logical-line assembly that tracks delimiters, recursive parsing for declarations, types and statements, and Pratt parsing with query continuations for expressions. Fully parse each supported field, type, attribute, body, example and route: neither retaining an unparsed remainder, skipping an unrecognized head nor using semantic resolution to choose AST shapes is acceptable. Run it against all 44 files and targeted cases for absent corpus features, including semicolon sequences, unions, field descriptions, context declarations, routes and migrations. Error reports must locate the file, line and column and say what was expected. Resolving names, imports and types, checking authority and constraints, implementing runtime behavior, and executing BDD cases remain future work. The missing mandatory fixture category in CanOnboard is still a semantic error. A successful syntax parse cannot establish complete language conformance or application correctness.
state.research: Use https://docs.python.org/3/reference/lexical_analysis.html as primary evidence about logical lines, continuation inside brackets and soft keywords, and https://github.com/munificent/craftinginterpreters/blob/master/book/parsing-expressions.md for recursive-descent AST construction and precedence handling. Reuse these techniques without importing Python's indentation or keyword rules. Relevant source observations are CanRent:49 for array concatenation together with inner and outer queries, ExpenseFlow:60 for the comma between a query and sum's second argument, CanMember:59 for the named fold argument, CanTable:59 for ordering a UI selector list, CanStock:57 for a local binding outside do, and ExpenseFlow:6-14 for a schema extending over physical lines. No source in the corpus contains semicolon sequences, unions, migrations or tabs, so it cannot by itself cover the entire proposed grammar.

code.query: all([from]+(resource.Booking as b where busy(b) select b.reserved_from) as point,quantity+sum(resource.Booking as b where b.reserved_from<=point select b.quantity)<=resource.capacity)
code.stock:
scenario post(item:Item,location:Location,value:StockReceipt) by=stock_staff
 require can_work(actor,location) and item.active and value.location==location.id and value.sku==item.sku and value.unit==item.unit and value.quantity>0
 let receipt=first(Receipt as receipt where receipt.source==value.source order=receipt.id)
 require receipt!=null and receipt.accepted==value.quantity and receipt.parent.sku==value.sku and receipt.parent.unit==value.unit and receipt.parent.parent.location==location and receipt.parent.parent.reference==value.order
 require not any(Movement as movement,movement.source==value.source)
 do create Movement {parent=item,location,quantity=value.quantity,reason="Accepted purchase receipt",source=value.source,order=value.order,actor} as movement

state.suffix_resolution: Treat suffix composition on a referenced field according to its eventual value shape. Wrapping a nullable value or array in [] is outside scope, and repeating nullable ? is an error. For a nonnullable array obtained by reuse, field ! may follow the path directly (items:Contract.rows!) and controls this declaration's creation requirement independently. Scalar builtins cannot take !; unbound qualified references await semantic checking.

query.instructions: Choose the single query notation most suitable for the given requirements on precise parsing and ease of adoption.

criteria.contextual_tail: Keep the existing loosely binding clauses in their fixed order, delimiting them precisely by surrounding context and parsing UI selector lists independently.
criteria.explicit_wrapper: Require query(...) in place of those clauses, making the boundary explicit while increasing syntax at every usage and requiring source changes.
criteria.unresolved: Withhold a selection when neither notation handles the shown expressions coherently.

types.instructions: Select the suffix and grouping rules that the first type grammar should establish.

criteria.flat_bounded: Limit values to unions of named paths, a single array suffix and subsequent container nullability; treat required-array notation solely as field metadata and disallow nesting whose contract has not been specified.
criteria.recursive_grouped: Specify recursive grouping, unions, arrays and nullable types immediately, admitting more complex structures while requiring more semantic definitions and implementation work.
criteria.unresolved: Leave the type-suffix decision unsettled if neither alternative meets the stated requirements.

reuse.instructions: Can one syntactic production for type paths, followed by semantic reuse of field value properties, form a coherent design while leaving creation rules, uniqueness and authority behind?

coherence.instructions: Do these rules for source layout, position-dependent words, expression/header/query limits and inline versus indented execution specify deterministic parsing for the proposed syntax AST implementation, which rejects invalid input instead of interpreting it speculatively?
